{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABc-sF0g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhGg800", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 109, "title": "Allow idle SMPC COMREG commands with SF=0 without implicitly setting SF", "body": "## Problem

A user with their own lawful 512 KiB Sega Saturn BIOS can now start the **User-provided BIOS** mode without a disc, but firmware execution stops with:

```text
Memory access at PC 0x0000025C:
SMPC COMREG 1-byte write at 0x2010001F value=0x0000001A:
MissingSf (SF=0, busy=false, command=0x00)
```

The decoded command `0x1A` is **RESDISA** (disable reset-button NMI). The user has **not supplied their proprietary BIOS**, and the preceding instruction trace is unavailable; no one should assume their specific earlier SF writes or a guaranteed stock BIOS menu outcome.

At current `main` `2127767b7e31cdd5fab386d7f147e28c43a13f7a`, `src/smpc.rs::Smpc::write_from` has a strict `0x1F if !self.sf => MissingSf` rule. This is intentionally described by [Issue #105](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/issues/105) as a **host protocol diagnostic**, **not** a verified electrical SMPC gate or an architectural SH-2 exception. #105 confirmed that the documented **SF-before-COMREG** sequence works, but did not change the rejection policy or fix real BIOS startup.

New external compatibility evidence motivates testing a narrower, different policy:

- [Mednafen SMPC implementation](https://github.com/OpenEmu/Mednafen-Core/blob/master/mednafen/ss/smpc.cpp), `SMPC_Write`: `case 0x0F` (COMREG) queues `PendingCommand = V` without checking `SF`, while `case 0x31` sets SF; completion clears it. It logs warnings for writes while a command is pending/executing. Register offsets are normalized and differ from the physical Saturn odd-byte offsets.
- [5thPlanet SMPC implementation](https://github.com/hiroshiyui/5thPlanet/blob/main/crates/saturn/src/smpc.rs): `write8(0x1F)` latches/queues the command without auto-setting SF, and `write8(0x63)` handles SF separately.
- [5thPlanet debugging case](https://github.com/hiroshiyui/5thPlanet/blob/main/doc/debugging-playbook.md): Greatest Nine '98 issued `SNDOFF (0x07)` without a preceding SF write; auto-setting SF on COMREG caused an infinite poll loop. Removing that automatic set fixed a game boot hang. This is **not** proof that the user's BIOS issues the exact same sequence.
- [Sega ST-169 SMPC User's Manual](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-169-R1-072694.pdf), §§1.2, 2.2–2.3: documents the software sequence of checking SF=0, setting SF=1, then issuing COMREG. It does **not** conclusively specify the electrical response to a COMREG write while SF=0.

These independent emulator precedents provide a credible **compatibility hypothesis**, not hardware measurement or a license to copy other projects' code.

## Expected outcome

Implement and verify a **small, source-authored change in the shared Saturn SMPC model**: when no command or INTBACK phase is active, allow a **valid, otherwise permitted 8-bit COMREG command** even if SF was never set, **without automatically setting SF**. The existing documented pre-write sequence must still work. The real command, pending/deadline, OREG31, reset-enable and other side effects must occur as usual, and the hardware must clear SF at completion. The model must not reinterpret SF itself as internal busy or force busy/readback to a fabricated value.

Retain distinct safeguards for unsupported/invalid commands and parameters, prohibited slave-CPU issuers, invalid access widths/lanes, read-only/write-only registers and actually busy/overlapping command processing. Do **not** turn every invalid SMPC write into success, install a workaround at PC `0x0000025C`, fake BIOS pixels, or bypass real guest execution.

**Scope:** test the SF=0 / idle COMREG acceptance policy in hardware code; not a broad SMPC rewrite or a claim of complete genuine BIOS/retail compatibility.

## Implementation guidance

1. Inspect `src/smpc.rs` COMREG branch ordering and `busy()`, `sf`, `pending`, command latching, `advance_clocks`, INTBACK and reset transitions. Separate **internal execution in progress** from **software's SF synchronization flag**. Remove/refine only the unconditional `MissingSf` idle rejection, preserving command validation and timing for both SF=0 and SF=1. Change relevant comments/diagnostics so they do not claim a measured hardware rejection.
2. Reuse the single command dispatch path for RESDISA `0x1A`, SNDOFF `0x07`, and other valid commands. Do not duplicate command tables, silently set `sf=true`, or change command duration, report and reset effects solely to pass the test.
3. Retain explicit deterministic policy on truly busy COMREG writes (currently `Busy`), including when SF was cleared or set independently; distinguish the software flag from pending/executing command state. Preserve known allowed INTBACK continue/BREAK semantics.
4. Use the external projects as evidence/comparison, not copied source. Explain which behavior is documented in Sega's manual and which is an emulator-compatibility interpretation.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Minimal source change:** an idle valid COMREG write is accepted with either `SF=0` or `SF=1`. `SF=0` acceptance does **not** implicitly turn SF on. `SF=1` stays observable until documented completion. Command completion clears SF in both cases, with the original deadline/side effect/OREG31 reporting preserved.
- [ ] **Actual RESDISA effects:** synthetic master SH-2 firmware with power-on SF=0 issues `0x1A` via `0x2010001F` and continues past the old `MissingSf` fault. Verify OREG31=1A, pending and completion, reset-button NMI disabled at the correct deadline (ideally first issue RESENAB to make the effect observable). Include `SF=1` pre-write control. No host-side guest memory/flag injection.
- [ ] **Non-pre-write SNDOFF and other representative commands:** test `SF=0` + `0x07` plus a single-read SF check, and at least one other existing valid command, with actual sound/CPU/IRQ or state consequences and timing. Prove no automatic SF=1 and no permanent poll loop; use original guest code, not a copyrighted game.
- [ ] **Robust negative controls:** duplicate COMREG during true internal busy remains rejected/handled according to an explicitly justified policy; invalid command and parameter payloads, prohibited slave issuers, invalid SF writes, bad MMIO widths/lanes and reads of write-only COMREG stay bounded and correctly diagnosed. No changes to CPU exception semantics or blanket swallowing of faults.
- [ ] **Reset and INTBACK invariants:** power/reset defaults, command completion, SF pre-write/poll sequence, timed reset/cancellation, INTBACK status/peripheral continuation/BREAK and SCU IRQ behavior remain correct; no double scheduling, spurious SMPC IRQ or stale pending command. Validate across small/large scheduler advancement chunks.
- [ ] **Native + production Wasm/browser tests:** add focused unit/native guest regressions with a redistributable synthetic 512 KiB BIOS and production Wasm/Chromium checks; use the existing `tests/fixtures/build_smpc_transactions.py`, `tests/smpc_transactions.rs`, `scripts/hardware-boundaries.mjs` / Play-UI path as appropriate. Demonstrate fail-before/pass-after for SF=0 idle valid write and preserve existing audio/media/BIOS-only UI tests.
- [ ] **Diagnostic/documentation update:** update `src/smpc/diagnostics.rs` expectations where appropriate and `docs/hardware-conformance.md`, `docs/validation-issue-105.md` (or a focused issue validation record). State explicitly that the SF=0 acceptance policy is supported by third-party emulator precedents but **not** verified as physical Saturn electrical behavior.
- [ ] **Full required validation:** run applicable fmt, locked Rust build/tests/Clippy, fixture check, Wasm build/Clippy, CI-runner regressions and all browser shards under current CI performance policy, without dropping tests, bumping timeouts, or weakening artifact/publication gates. Require passing exact-head PR checks before merge.

## BIOS compatibility check by the user (optional after the implementation is available)

The requester **will personally test their lawful Sega BIOS** after the change is published/deployed, and may report whether the original `0x0000025C` fault disappears and what later hardware access, if any, fails. The implementation owner **does not have and must not require that BIOS or its bytes**. Do not make the user's private verification, the stock BIOS menu, human confirmation, live Pages deployment, or gameplay a pre-merge gate. If further failures appear, pursue them as separate evidence-based hardware issues instead of applying ROM/PC-specific patches.

## Required post-merge verification

None as an implementation acceptance gate. The user's real-BIOS smoke test is separate, voluntary feedback.
